context:
Goal: a lane brief tells the lane who to message, and the ids it names do not go stale.
Problem (rule): two of your rules disagree. R22 (your words 19:19 CST Nov 10, after a respawn left old session ids everywhere) says point 3: a page item, brief or handoff names a lane slug or role, never a session id. The roadmap branch's CLAUDE.md roster header says: "Lane briefs name these ids. Triage rewrites a line when a role changes hands." So one tells briefs to carry ids and the other forbids it. The new check in PR #3352 (brief-ids-in-roster) and its record, docs/decisions/brief-ids-in-roster.md, state both and settle neither. The roster line is triage's own file; triage will not edit it without your word.
Based on (read): ruling R22 point 3 (read by triage); the roster header in the roadmap CLAUDE.md (read by triage); lane brief-ids-from-roster's note, 00:05 CST, unchecked.
Departs from: main — the check lets a brief carry an id that is in the roster; a keeps that (the ids in the roster, rewritten by triage on a respawn); b makes briefs name a slug or role only.
Meanwhile: nothing changes; PR #3352 states both and is not blocked on this.
home: ruling R22 (point 3); roadmap branch CLAUDE.md, Standing sessions; PR #3352; docs/decisions/brief-ids-in-roster.md
lastAnswer: 819: b, a brief names a slug or role only (00:19 CST Nov 14).

options.gain: A lane can message the coordinator or triage straight from its brief; one roster is the only source of ids.
options.label: A brief may name a standing session by the id in the roster, which triage rewrites on a respawn; R22 point 3 is narrowed to ids not in the roster
options.lose: R22 point 3 is narrowed; a missed roster rewrite leaves a stale id again.

options.gain: A respawn cannot leave a stale id in a brief.
options.label: A brief names a slug or role only; the lane looks the id up in the roster (R22 point 3 as written)
options.lose: Every lane needs one more read to find an id; the roster header and the check in #3352 change.

reply: Closed on your b. Filed as ruling own-819-b-slug-or-role. A brief names a lane slug or role only, never a session id; the lane looks the id up in the roster. The roster header in the roadmap branch's CLAUDE.md is rewritten to say so. Lane brief-ids-from-roster changes its check in PR #3352 and its decision record to match.
short: Brief naming session ids: roster header or R22 point 3?
title: Your rule R22 says briefs never carry a session id, but the roster header says they name the roster's ids. Which stands?
why: Two of your own words disagree; only you settle which.
